patent.title: Method for node ranking in a linked database
assignees: The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University
patent.family_note: Same patent observed at two historical T0 dates. Current legal-status labels are not backfilled into either historical state.

knowledge_origin.description: Public filings identify PageRank as developed at Stanford by Google's founders and the PageRank patent as Stanford-owned.

technology.problem: Rank web pages in a linked database to improve the relevance and usefulness of search results.
technology.mechanism: A query-independent node-ranking method that uses link structure to estimate page importance and is combined with other ranking and text-matching techniques in Google search.
technology.comparison_baseline: Contemporaneous web-search ranking approaches; this ledger does not perform a field-normalized prior-art score.

value_carriers.name: Google Web Search ranking system
value_carriers.description: Google's public filing directly identifies PageRank as one element of its ranking technology.

value_links.note: The patent maps to a component of the ranking system, not to the entire Google search or advertising stack.

value_metrics.note: Enterprise value context only; no patent-level attribution.

value_metrics.value: exclusive license through 2011; patent stated to expire in 2017
value_metrics.note: A rights-horizon fact, not a monetary patent valuation.

gaps.description: Google's enterprise revenue, traffic and search scale cannot be apportioned to US6285999 from the public record.

V0.7 does not separately represent accumulated revealed-value history, remaining exclusive-license duration, remaining patent term, or future option horizon; therefore two T0 states can both appear as R4 despite materially different asset horizons.

notes: Two-clock experiment at T0=2004-08-04. exclusive license through 2011; patent stated to expire in 2017. R4 records implemented/scale state only; it must not be read as a constant value score across time.
